expectedText:
REPRODUCTIVE LOSS LEAVE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

REPRODUCTIVE LOSS LEAVE ENTITLEMENT
Under California law, it is an unlawful employment practice for a covered employer to refuse a covered employee's request to take up to five days of reproductive loss leave following a reproductive loss event. The days taken need not be consecutive. If an employee experiences more than one reproductive loss event within a 12-month period, the employer is not obligated to grant more than a combined total of 20 days of reproductive loss leave within that 12-month period.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "It shall be an unlawful employment practice for an employer to refuse to grant a request by any employee to take up to five days of reproductive loss leave following a reproductive loss event. If an employee experiences more than one reproductive loss event within a 12-month period, an employer shall not be obligated to grant a total amount of reproductive loss leave time in excess of 20 days within a 12-month period."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(b)(1), core entitlement and 20-day cap (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "The employer shall allow the days an employee takes for reproductive loss leave to be nonconsecutive."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(b)(2), nonconsecutive days (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  Known gap: The statute caps combined reproductive loss leave at 20 days within a 12-month period when an employee has more than one qualifying event, but it does not itself state whether that 12-month period is measured as a rolling 12 months from a given event or a fixed 12-month period (such as a calendar or employer-designated leave year); this document does not resolve that ambiguity.

DEFINITION OF A REPRODUCTIVE LOSS EVENT
A "reproductive loss event" is the day of, or for a multiple-day event the final day of, a failed adoption, a failed surrogacy, a miscarriage, a stillbirth, or an unsuccessful assisted reproduction. "Assisted reproduction" means a method of achieving a pregnancy through an artificial insemination or an embryo transfer, and includes gamete and embryo donation, but does not include any pregnancy achieved through sexual intercourse; "unsuccessful assisted reproduction" means an unsuccessful round of intrauterine insemination or of an assisted reproductive technology procedure. Each of these terms extends to an event experienced by the employee, by the employee's current spouse or domestic partner, or by another individual, where the employee would have been a parent of the child involved.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "“Reproductive loss event” means the day or, for a multiple-day event, the final day of a failed adoption, failed surrogacy, miscarriage, stillbirth, or an unsuccessful assisted reproduction."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(a)(7), definition of “reproductive loss event” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "“Assisted reproduction” means a method of achieving a pregnancy through an artificial insemination or an embryo transfer and includes gamete and embryo donation."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(a)(1), definition of “assisted reproduction” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "“Unsuccessful assisted reproduction” means an unsuccessful round of intrauterine insemination or of an assisted reproductive technology procedure."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(a)(10), definition of “unsuccessful assisted reproduction” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "“Failed adoption” means the dissolution or breach of an adoption agreement with the birth mother or legal guardian, or an adoption that is not finalized because it is contested by another party."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(a)(4)-(5), definitions of “failed adoption” and “failed surrogacy” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  Known gap: This is a research correction to a common shorthand: the statute does not use the phrase "IVF" or limit "unsuccessful assisted reproduction" to in vitro fertilization — the statutory term is broader, covering any unsuccessful round of intrauterine insemination or of an assisted reproductive technology procedure, without itself defining what qualifies as an "assisted reproductive technology procedure." This document does not independently verify that term against any separate statute or regulation that might define it.

EMPLOYEE ELIGIBILITY AND EMPLOYER COVERAGE
For purposes of this leave, an "employee" is a person who has been employed by the employer for at least 30 days before the leave begins. This requirement applies to an "employer," defined as a person who employs five or more persons to perform services for a wage or salary, as well as to the state and any of its political or civil subdivisions, including cities and counties.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "“Employee” means a person employed by the employer for at least 30 days prior to the commencement of the leave."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(a)(2), definition of “employee” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "“Employer” means either of the following: (A) A person who employs five or more persons to perform services for a wage or salary. (B) The state and any political or civil subdivision of the state, including, but not limited to, cities and counties."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(a)(3), definition of “employer” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  Known gap: These employee and employer definitions are worded identically to the ones used in California's bereavement leave statute (Gov. Code § 12945.7), but they are separately defined within this section; this document does not assume that a determination made under one leave statute automatically controls the other, only that the operative text is the same.

TIMING OF LEAVE AND INTERACTION WITH OTHER LEAVE
Reproductive loss leave generally must be completed within three months of the reproductive loss event. If, before or immediately after the event, the employee is on or chooses to go on leave under Government Code § 12945 (relating to pregnancy disability), § 12945.2 (the California Family Rights Act), or any other state or federal leave entitlement, the three-month window instead runs from the end date of that other leave.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Except as provided in subparagraph (B), reproductive loss leave shall be completed within three months of the event entitling the employee to that leave under paragraph (1)."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(b)(3)(A), general three-month completion window (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "Notwithstanding subparagraph (A), if, prior to or immediately following a reproductive loss event, an employee is on or chooses to go on leave from work pursuant to Section 12945, 12945.2, or any other leave entitlement under state or federal law, the employee shall complete their reproductive loss leave within three months of the end date of the other leave."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(b)(3)(B), extension when combined with other leave (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  Known gap: This clause states that the three-month window can be extended by an overlapping leave under § 12945, § 12945.2, or another leave entitlement, but it does not independently restate or verify the eligibility rules, duration, or scope of those other leave laws; they are addressed, where covered, in this corpus's separate documents on pregnancy disability leave and the California Family Rights Act.

PAID OR UNPAID STATUS OF THE LEAVE
Reproductive loss leave is taken under the employer's own existing applicable leave policy, if it has one. If the employer has no existing applicable leave policy, the leave may be unpaid, except that the employee may use vacation, personal leave, accrued and available sick leave, or compensatory time off that is otherwise available.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Reproductive loss leave shall be taken pursuant to any existing applicable leave policy of the employer."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(b)(4)(A), leave taken under employer's existing policy (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "If there is no existing applicable leave policy, reproductive loss leave may be unpaid, except that an employee may use vacation, personal leave, accrued and available sick leave, or compensatory time off that is otherwise available to the employee."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(b)(4)(B), default unpaid status absent an employer policy (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  Known gap: The statute does not create a freestanding state-paid reproductive loss leave benefit; payment, where it exists, comes from the employer's own policy or the employee's own accrued paid leave. This document does not address whether a separate wage-replacement program, such as State Disability Insurance, may apply to the underlying medical event itself, since that is a different program not created or modified by this leave statute.

CONFIDENTIALITY, ANTI-RETALIATION, AND INDEPENDENCE FROM OTHER RIGHTS
The employer must maintain the confidentiality of any employee requesting leave under this statute, and any information provided to the employer under this section must be kept confidential and disclosed only to internal personnel or counsel as necessary, or as otherwise required by law. It is a separate unlawful employment practice for an employer to retaliate against an individual — including by refusing to hire, discharging, demoting, fining, suspending, expelling, or discriminating against them — because the individual exercised the right to reproductive loss leave or gave information or testimony about their own or someone else's reproductive loss leave in a related inquiry or proceeding, and it is likewise unlawful for an employer to interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of any right this section provides. An employee's right to reproductive loss leave is a separate and distinct right from any other right under this part of the Government Code.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The employer shall maintain the confidentiality of any employee requesting leave under this section. Any information provided to the employer pursuant to this section shall be maintained as confidential and shall not be disclosed except to internal personnel or counsel, as necessary, or as required by law."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(e), confidentiality (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "It shall be an unlawful employment practice for an employer to retaliate against an individual, including, but not limited to, refusing to hire, discharging, demoting, fining, suspending, expelling, or discriminating against, an individual because of either of the following: (1) An individual’s exercise of the right to reproductive loss leave."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(c), retaliation for exercising or discussing reproductive loss leave rights (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "It shall be an unlawful employment practice for an employer to interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of, or the attempt to exercise, any right provided under this section."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(d), interference with the right to reproductive loss leave (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  "An employee’s right to reproductive loss leave shall be construed as a separate and distinct right from any right under this part."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6 (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov), Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.6(f), leave is a separate and distinct right (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.6)
  Known gap: Unlike California's bereavement leave statute (Gov. Code § 12945.7(f)), this reproductive loss leave statute does not include a provision expressly authorizing the employer to request supporting documentation of the event within a set number of days. This document does not conclude from that silence that an employer has, or lacks, any documentation right under this section; it states only that the statute itself does not spell one out the way the bereavement leave statute does.

REPRODUCTIVE LOSS LEAVE REQUEST
Jordan Lee requests reproductive loss leave from Acme, Inc. as described below.

Type of reproductive loss event (failed adoption, failed surrogacy, miscarriage, stillbirth, or unsuccessful assisted reproduction): _______________________________________________
Date of the event (for a multiple-day event, the final day): _______________
Dates of leave requested (need not be consecutive): _______________________________________________
Total days requested (up to 5 for this event; up to 20 total in a 12-month period if this is not the employee's only reproductive loss event in that period): _______________
Jordan Lee understands that Acme, Inc. must maintain the confidentiality of this request and of any information provided in connection with it, and will not be disclosed except to internal personnel or counsel as necessary, or as required by law.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to acknowledge this reproductive loss leave request and the terms above.

Employee: Jordan Lee
Date: _______________
